about: Layer-2 conformance probes for dashscene's SDF shader library: the inputs, the expected values and the tolerances, so a painter in any shading language can check the same mathematics. See conformance/README.md.
properties: docs/design/dashscene-gpu.md — 'The probe table, and what stays a property'. This file carries only the claims that are one value at one input; the rest a painter must implement as properties.

functions.name: clamp_radii
functions.reference: independent — the over-subscription rule, restated per edge

functions.name: rounded_box_sdf
functions.signature: rounded_box_sdf(p: vec2f, half_size: vec2f, radii: vec4f) -> f32
functions.reference: independent — brute-force sampling of the outline; the tolerance is 1.6 times the 0.0122 sample spacing, which is the bound that always holds

functions.name: coverage
functions.reference: transliterated — the ramp is its own definition, so this checks the transliteration and not the mathematics

functions.name: median3
functions.reference: independent — a sort, rather than the shader's min/max lattice

functions.name: msdf_coverage
functions.reference: independent for the median, transliterated for the ramp it is composed with

functions.name: gradient_linear_t
functions.signature: gradient_linear_t(p: vec2f, origin: vec2f, primary: vec2f, secondary: vec2f) -> f32
functions.reference: transliterated — the parameterization is its own definition

functions.name: gradient_radial_t
functions.signature: gradient_radial_t(p: vec2f, origin: vec2f, primary: vec2f, secondary: vec2f) -> f32
functions.reference: transliterated — the parameterization is its own definition

functions.name: gradient_angular_t
functions.signature: gradient_angular_t(p: vec2f, origin: vec2f, primary: vec2f, secondary: vec2f) -> f32
functions.reference: transliterated — the parameterization is its own definition

functions.name: gradient_diamond_t
functions.signature: gradient_diamond_t(p: vec2f, origin: vec2f, primary: vec2f, secondary: vec2f) -> f32
functions.reference: transliterated — the parameterization is its own definition

functions.name: gradient_ramp
functions.signature: gradient_ramp(t: f32, offsets: array<f32, 8>, colours: array<vec4f, 8>, count: u32) -> vec4f
functions.reference: independent — the first stop past t and the segment before it, rather than the shader's overwriting walk

functions.name: stroke_coverage
functions.signature: stroke_coverage(d: f32, width: f32, align: f32, aa: f32) -> f32
functions.reference: independent in form — the band's overlap with the pixel footprint, rather than the shader's difference of two edge ramps. The two are algebraically equal for a linear ramp, so this checks the arrangement rather than adding a second derivation: the folded single ramp the shader used before story #579 fails it, a faithful port does not

functions.name: erf_approx
functions.reference: independent — erf's own definition, integrated by Simpson's rule in double precision; the tolerance is the accuracy the fitted form is trusted within (docs/decisions/shader-library-and-layer-2.md)

functions.name: blurred_rounded_box
functions.signature: blurred_rounded_box(p: vec2f, half_size: vec2f, radii: vec4f, sigma: f32) -> f32
functions.reference: independent — a 512-row quadrature with an integrated erf, against the shader's twelve rows and a fitted one, except at sigma = 0 where both answer the unblurred shape and neither integrates; the tolerance is D5's budget of one code point of an eight-bit channel
